messages.subject: Horizontal bar chart + facet_grid
parts:
I want to plot horizontal bar chart by categorizing datasets.

name, grade, section
student1, 56, A
student2, 68, A
student3, 58, A
student4, 99, B
student5, 46, C
student6, 44, C
student7, 34, C
student8, 56, C
student9, 76, C

(In dot plot)
I can plot nicely with dotplot with following command.
>qplot(grade, name, data=test, color=section)+ facet_grid(section ~ ., scales="free",space="free")

(In barchart)
>ggplot(data=test, aes(x=name, y=grade))+geom_bar()+coord_flip()+facet_grid( section ~., scales="free", space="free")

I got 3 panels with own scale not like in the dot plot.
How can I plot horizontal bar chart without changing y-axis (I want to
maintain this y-axis)?

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: Horizontal bar chart + facet_grid
parts:
Strange. I confirmed this, making sure that ggplot2 was at version
0.8.2. This is very similar to the issue I had a while back and
Hadley pointed out that I wasn't using scales and space right, but
even with the new version and without cood_flip(), I see the same issue.

td <- read.csv(textConnection("name,grade,section
student1,56,A
student2,68,A
student3,58,A
student4,99,B
student5,46,C
student6,44,C
student7,34,C
student8,56,C
student9,76,C"))
closeAllConnections()

# without coord__flip(), we want the x axis to vary for the plots.
ggplot(data=td, aes(x=name, y=grade))+geom_bar()+facet_grid( section
~., scales="free_x", space="free")

But this produces the same X axis (ie all students) for each graph. On
the other hand "free_y" seems to work without problems:

ggplot(data=td, aes(x=name, y=grade))+geom_bar()+facet_grid( section
~., scales="free_y", space="free")

This has graphs with the Y scales different (probably bad, but worth
trying ;)

--J

If possible I think it should be consistent with the idea that
coord_flip() is the last thing you add. ie build the plot with
regular orientation, then apply coord_flip(). So the 'x' and 'y' axes
should refer to the situation without coord_flip(). That's what
happens with, for example, labeling the axes at the moment (eg
scale_y_continuous(name="Y axis")+coord_flip() puts that label on the
horizontal axis).

For that reason I think that scales="free_y" should do the same, after
coord_flip() that means that the horizontal axis scale is free. With
scales="free" it's not going to matter. Or am I missing something?

Cheers,
James

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d

parts:
> If possible I think it should be consistent with the idea that
> coord_flip() is the last thing you add.  ie build the plot with
> regular orientation, then apply coord_flip().  So the 'x' and 'y' axes
> should refer to the situation without coord_flip().  That's what
> happens with, for example, labeling the axes at the moment (eg
> scale_y_continuous(name="Y axis")+coord_flip() puts that label on the
> horizontal axis).

The problem is that coord_flip() isn't necessarily the last thing you
add. i.e. you could do:

+ coord_flip()
+ facet_grid()

which should have the same effect as the opposite order (or at least I
think it should, based on the current principle that only the ordering
of the layers makes any difference to the final plot)

> For that reason I think that scales="free_y" should do the same, after
> coord_flip() that means that the horizontal axis scale is free.  With
> scales="free" it's not going to matter.  Or am I missing something?

I think that makes sense, but it's not obvious to me (yet) how to code
that, and how it should work in general for all coordinate systems.

Regards,

Hadley

messages.author: 519455d3bf64680d
messages.subject: A question and answer template for GGPLOT inquiries
parts:
As part of the ggplot community, I'm proposing that we work toward a
standardized template to structure future user questions. The idea is
not that the template is mandatory, but that it would help users
articulate their questions more completely (and maybe encourage
self-discover of answers!)

I have spoke with Hadley about this, and I'd welcome assistance and
suggestions directly to me (rob at aetiologic dot ca ) that I could
include in the template. What are the essential elements in attempting
to answer a user query?

If we can find two or three other folks who would work with me to build
that template (or have other similar ideas!), then maybe we can reduce
the demand on Hadley and improve the value of responses. I cannot but
imagine that traffic on this group is going to grow quickly as word of
ggplot gets out, so setting up a standard format may be essential to
managing future inquiry demands.

Rob James

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: A question and answer template for GGPLOT inquiries
parts:
I like this idea a lot. Here's a suggested template, just to get the
ball rolling.

==Goal:

I'm trying to ..., so I can communicate ...

==Minimal Sample Data:

inline using textConnection(). eg:

testdata <- read.csv(textConnection("

name,grade,section
student1,56,A
student2,68,A
student3,58,A
student4,99,B

student9,76,C

"))
closeAllConnections()

(just tested and the extra line breaks get ignored there, which helps
readability).

==Minimal Code:

Copy and pastable ggplot2 commands (excluding library(ggplot2) but
including loading any other needed libraries. Knowing what version
people are using is crucial, the line below does it, but someone
better at R can probably make that neater, maybe ggplot2 could have a
function to show its version?

as.data.frame(installed.packages())["ggplot2",]$Version
qplot(data=testdata, ...

or

ggplot(data=testdata, ... + ....


==Output

Copy in the output from R that you see (including the Version of
ggplot that the line above prints out)

((Ok, where it gets a little tricky in email is in showing the plot
and what's wrong with it. Ideally one would paste a link to the
figure with the ability to highlight/circle parts. Does anyone know
of a pastie style website that would allow something so cool?))

Or do we just want to allow posting pics to the email; it's not a hugh
imposition!

==What I want or expected

I was hoping to get the label "xyz" for the x axis.

---------------

We should also refer people to ESR's "How to ask questions the smart
way" a lot, especially the bits about *followup* and complete, minimal

http://www.catb.org/~esr/faqs/smart-questions.html

Andy Seaborne has a nice definition of complete, minimal:

Complete => standalone code than can be run
Minimal => only contains code or data relevant to the question.

Replies should include lots of pointers to the documentation on the
ggplot2 website and the book, but also mostly executable code :) We
could nominate techniques etc for adding to the documentation of
particular elements?

--J
